name: Electrolytic Bone Density Projector EBDP-4 'Chalk'
description: The EBDP-4 delivers a pulsed electrolytic field tuned to disrupt the calcium hydroxyapatite mineral matrix of cortical bone. Rather than fracturing bone mechanically, the weapon induces rapid electrolytic demineralization — stripping calcium ions from the bone lattice through a process similar to accelerated osteoclast activity compressed into milliseconds. The result is a localized region of catastrophically weakened bone that fails under normal mechanical load, causing compound fractures from the target's own movement or the force of incidental contact.
specifications: length: 55 cm weight: 2.8 kg power source: Helix BioElec HBE-7 dual-cell effective range: 6–70 m pulse frequency: 3.4 MHz electrolytic field demineralization onset: Immediate on sustained hit (0.3 second minimum) target bone density reduction: 60–80% in affected region per full pulse shots per cell: 18 full pulses chassis: Medical-grade polymer housing (repurposed surgical device chassis)
tactical_use: The EBDP-4 is used almost exclusively in ambush and assassination contexts. Operators typically deliver a pulse to a load-bearing structure — femur, tibia, or lumbar vertebrae — and then allow the target to continue moving until natural biomechanical stress causes the weakened bone to fail. The delayed collapse window (2–15 seconds of continued movement) allows an operator to disengage before the target falls, making attribution difficult. Some operators use it to pre-weaken a target before a physical confrontation, ensuring that even minor strikes will cause catastrophic structural failure.
cultural_context: The EBDP-4 originated as a Helix Biosystems prototype for non-invasive bone density correction in degenerative disease patients — the demineralization function was intended to prepare bone tissue for remineralization therapy. The weaponized version surfaced on the black market roughly eighteen months after the prototype was shelved, suggesting an inside leak. In GLMZ's underworld, being hit by Chalk is considered one of the most humiliating ways to be taken down — experienced criminals read the injury pattern and know the target was marked in advance, implying either betrayal or surveillance. Helix Biosystems publicly denies any connection to the weapon.
story_hooks: A series of seemingly accidental falls and sports injuries among mid-level corporate managers are revealed to be EBDP-4 attacks — someone is running a long-term removal campaign designed to look like a bad luck streak.

A black-market dealer offers the party a EBDP-4 unit, but the weapon's internal logs contain targeting data for dozens of past operations — a treasure trove of evidence and a death sentence if the wrong people find out they have it.

Helix Biosystems hires the party to locate and destroy all existing EBDP-4 units before a regulatory investigation connects the weapon's design to their shelved medical prototype — but the party discovers the weapons were deliberately leaked by a Helix executive.

A player character begins experiencing unexplained bone fractures from minor impacts — a delayed-onset EBDP-4 pulse delivered days earlier is slowly destroying their skeletal structure, and they need the specific Helix antidote protocol before it reaches the spine.
ammunition_type: Helix Biosystems Compact Power Cell HB-3

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, medical-instrument-turned-weapon with an ergonomic surgical aesthetic. Resembles a high-end diagnostic probe or therapeutic device rather than conventional gunware—deliberately deceptive. Tapered, almost organic curves suggest biotech origin. The barrel is narrow and recessed, with a faint ionization glow visible in dim light.
physical_description.dimensions: 55 cm length overall; barrel depth 8 cm; grip width 4.2 cm; profile roughly 12 cm at widest (rear capacitor housing)
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light and balanced despite internal power cells—2.8 kg distributes toward the rear, making it point-light and controllable in one hand. Feels like holding a high-end medical scanner rather than lethal hardware.
physical_description.primary_material: Medical-grade polymer housing (white/translucent composite) over carbon-fiber reinforced skeleton. Internal architecture visible through frosted polymer panels on the rear capacitor assembly.
physical_description.finish: Matte translucent white polymer with brushed stainless steel accents. Internal circuitry and dual-cell power core slightly visible through panel seams—a design choice that reads as professional rather than militaristic. Minimal paint; most surfaces are bare composite.
physical_description.color_scheme: Clinical white and ice-blue primary; stainless steel secondary accents. Faint cyan glow from active capacitor cells visible through rear housing panels. No tactical black or drab finishes—the weapon deliberately mimics medical equipment.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured medical-grade silicone wrapped around the rear grip section. Slightly tacky, designed for precision control during extended use. Finger grooves are subtle and anatomically refined.
distinctive_features: Recessed ionization barrel with faint blue corona discharge visible when armed
Dual-cell HBE-7 power core visible through translucent rear panel with blue electrolyte glow
Frequency calibration dial (3.4 MHz marking) on the left side grip
Minimal sighting system—optical targeting reticle on top rail, sleek and low-profile
Heat-dissipation vents along the barrel shroud (surgical cooling design, not tactical)
Pulse-feedback indicator lights (cyan LED) on the capacitor housing, stepping up in intensity during charge cycle
No visible safety selector—safety is likely biometric or firmware-locked
Wear-resistant nano-coating on barrel tip—almost invisible, but catches light with an oil-slick iridescence
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo (double helix in chrome) stamped on the left side of the capacitor housing. Serial number engraved on a small stainless steel plate recessed into the grip. Regulatory/hazard markings in small text on the barrel shroud (barely visible, clinical rather than tactical).
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units range from pristine to lightly worn. Some show discoloration around the barrel tip from electrolytic discharge residue (faint mineral staining). Grip silicone may show minor scuffs. Operators maintain these meticulously—they're surgical instruments first, weapons second. Black-market units sometimes show jury-rigged modifications to the targeting system or power cell housing.
